glossary.definition: Quantization shrinks an AI model by storing its internal numbers with less precision, trading a small amount of accuracy for a model that's significantly smaller and faster to run, sometimes even on a phone. It's similar to saving a photo as a smaller, more compressed file: some fine detail is lost, but for most everyday purposes it still looks essentially the same while taking up a fraction of the space.

items.title: OpenAI announces three big science discoveries and a new way to work with academics
items.summary: Less than a month after its mass release of hundreds of manuscripts that it said contained solutions to long-standing mathematics questions, OpenAI is back with three more "major" discoveries in math, computer science, and physics . What's different this time is the choice to have external experts that OpenAI describes as "shepherds" guiding the results in computer science and physics, while for the math problem it says that they advised it to release the AI output for researchers to work through their own explanations. Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation. This time OpenAI says it’s taking new advice from scientists on how to release the results.

items.title: What to watch for as enterprises move from AI experimentation to autonomous operations
items.summary: For the past three years, the enterprise artificial intelligence conversation has focused on what models can say. The next three years will be about what systems are allowed to do. That’s a harder problem that better models alone won’t solve. On Wednesday, Oct. 28, I’ll be in Boston for the Bloomberg Tech Event: Building the Agentic Enterprise , sponsored by Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.

items.title: Why Anthropic’s IPO Prospectus Is Missing So Many Key Figures
items.summary: Anthropic’s S-1 filing is hundreds of pages long—and it leaves out quite a few financial details. “Anthropic owes investors more information,” one analyst tells WIRED. Anthropic filed its hotly anticipated IPO prospectus on Monday, spelling out parts of the company’s business, strategy, and risk profile ahead of its public debut. Though the filing, known as an S-1, is several hundred pages long, it has some notable omissions—namely, certain financial figures.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra halves OpenAI's API prices and still gains ground on its larger models
items.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-6.1 Terra, a mid-range model that cuts API prices in half compared to its predecessor. Analysts say it sets a new standard for intelligence per dollar, especially for everyday computing tasks and AI-driven computer control. OpenAI has released GPT-6.1 Terra, a model it says pushes the cost-to-performance boundary further than any of its predecessors. API prices are half those of GPT-5.6 Terra.

items.title: Anthropic maintains its focus on safety in IPO filing
items.summary: Anthropic structured its corporate voting power in a special LLC to maintain its mission of building safe AI technology.

items.title: Will the real Anthropic please stand up
items.summary: After weeks of frenzied speculation, Anthropic has filed its IPO prospectus. The 335-page document (100 pages or so are focused on risks) lays out the company’s unique view of the technology it is building and the ways it believes it will change the world. But Anthropic has been honing its storytelling skills for years. In fact, its public messaging is a master class in narrative capture.

items.title: Anthropic’s IPO filing reveals its strategy for keeping enterprise customers hooked
items.summary: Anthropic’s S-1 shows more than half of its $100,000-plus customers now use both the Claude Platform and a first-party app, a cross-selling playbook reminiscent of Amazon that’s making enterprise customers stickier. Anthropic is building the same kind of cross-product ecosystem that helped make tech companies like Amazon and Uber enormously sticky, and its S-1 suggests the strategy is working. More than half of customers spending at least $100,000 annually now use both the Claude platform and a first-party app like Claude Code or Cowork, up from about 30% at the end of last year. “The speed and depth of our enterprise customer adoption are powerful evidence of Claude’s position at the frontier of AI,” the S-1, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday , reads.

items.title: SpaceX locks in $40B GPU financing deal with Apollo
items.summary: The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets. SpaceX has reached a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing for AI chips and related data center equipment, the company  disclosed in a regulatory filing Monday . In a statement, SpaceX called the deal the  “largest committed GPU financing” . Under the agreement, an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, the New York-based private equity giant, will buy the chips and related server hardware, then lease the equipment to SpaceX.

items.title: Microsoft Teams to get AI protection against phishing and fraud
items.summary: Microsoft is adding a new AI-powered security feature to Teams aimed at detecting phishing, scams, and identity theft by analyzing conversations, Bleeping Computer reports. Instead of primarily checking for malicious links and files, the tool will be able to identify suspicious behavior in the messages themselves, Microsoft said. The feature will primarily be used for new contacts, as they pose a higher security risk. The new security feature follows earlier warnings from Microsoft about attackers impersonating help desk staff in Teams to trick users into granting them remote access.

items.title: Oracle adds a semantic layer to ground AI agents in the business context
items.summary: Oracle is expanding its Autonomous AI Lakehouse with a Business Semantic Layer designed to give AI agents a consistent understanding of enterprise data, a move aimed at improving the accuracy of AI-generated insights and helping organizations scale agentic applications across business functions. To ground AI agents in business context, the Business Semantic Layer uses catalog annotations, SQL annotations imported from Oracle AI Database, and AI-suggested analytic views to create reusable models of enterprise data that capture dimensions, measures, hierarchies, calculations, and key performance indicators (KPIs), Oracle said in a statement. These models can then be used across Oracle’s natural-language querying, data retrieval, and analytics capabilities, including Select AI, to help ensure that queries and insights are based on consistent business definitions. Oracle said that the new capabilities will be available within the next 12 months.

items.title: Bihar Partners with IT Cos to Train Government School Teachers In AI
items.summary: Bihar’s Education Department has partnered with 11 IT firms, including Google Education, to equip government school teachers with skills in artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies. The initiative will receive support from the Union government’s skill development department and include practical IT training. It is part of Bihar’s broader plan to expand digital learning, including making computer education compulsory from Class 6 in government schools from the next academic session and introducing smart classrooms in 700 model schools. Bihar Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari said the training would prioritise AI, with the aim of improving teaching quality, according to Dainik Jagran.

items.title: Meta Wants $95 Billion Through Stock Sales to Fund AI Infrastructure
items.summary: Meta Platforms plans to raise up to $95 billion through equity offerings. This includes $35 billion in immediate public offerings of common and convertible preferred stock and a separate programme to sell up to $60 billion in shares. The company said the financing would support investments in AI infrastructure, computing capacity and personal superintelligence as it expands its AI products and services. Meta Investor NVIDIA, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Broadcom have indicated an interest in purchasing up to $5 billion collectively in the Class A offering.
